body:
Without looking at this issue too closely just yet, I have a feeling that this will be related to the lack of `first_time_kinematic` in the Jolt implementation, as talked about [here](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/109885#issuecomment-3218148168).

Also, here's a version of the MRP that doesn't require .NET:  [jolt-reparenting-issue.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23725578/jolt-reparenting-issue.zip)

Upon further investigation, it seems this doesn't really have much to do with `first_time_kinematic` after all.

The actual problem seems to be that the current implementation of `Node3D::reparent` isn't great for how kinematic bodies deal with transform changes.

If we assume an even simpler repro, where the `CharacterBody3D` starts out as already parented to the `RigidBody3D`, and all we do is reparent it to the scene root, this is what happens during the reparenting:

1. The current global transform of the body is stored in a temporary variable.
2. The body is removed from its current parent and thus removed from the physics world.
3. The body is added to its new parent, in this case the scene root, thus adding it back to the physics world.
    - The initial transform that gets set as part of adding it back to the physics world is the body's global transform at this time, which is just its local transform, since we haven't actually restored the global transform yet. The local (now global) transform happens to be within the `Area3D`.
5. The previous global transform is restored.
    - Since we're already in the physics world at this point, this gets treated as a movement from the previous transform (the initial transform) to the new transform, so the new transform isn't actually set, it's just cached for calculating the velocity at the next physics step.
7. The physics world is stepped, triggering a collision between the `CharacterBody3D` and the `Area3D` and then actually moving the `CharacterBody3D`.

The only reason this works in Godot Physics is because Godot Physics actually fails to initialize its cached transform (`GodotBody3D::new_transform`) when the `CharacterBody3D` is removed from and added back into the physics world, so by the time it performs the kinematic movement it's done from a stale value that just so happens to be where we wanted to move it, thereby effectively becoming a no-op.

I have a couple of solutions in mind, but none of them are very good:

1. Do [this](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a3e84cc2af14aa4cffbefd8e13492e59567a64e3/scene/3d/node_3d.cpp#L1029) inbetween [these two](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/blob/a3e84cc2af14aa4cffbefd8e13492e59567a64e3/scene/main/node.cpp#L2081-L2082) lines instead, but I don't see how that's possible without some ugly refactoring.
2. Instead of `Node3D::reparent` caching and restoring the previous global transform, just set its local transform in such a way that it ends up in the correct spot after reparenting.
3. Have `CollisionObject3D` override `Node3D::reparent` and temporarily set `DISABLE_MODE_REMOVE` and `PROCESS_MODE_DISABLE` for the entire duration of `Node3D::reparent`, and finish off with a `force_update_transform()`, thereby preventing the borked initial transform.

> I have a couple of solutions in mind, but none of them are very good:

I went ahead and pushed a PR with solution 2, since that seemed like the lesser evil, but I'm not happy about it: #113287
Any updates? Got this issue still in Godot v4.7

I haven't tested it, but I suspect that #113784 might also solve this problem, by letting us call this new `flush_kinematic_transform` method to forcefully move the kinematic body in something like `CollisionObject3D::reparent`. So getting that merged might also allow this to be fixed in a cleaner way than #113287 (which likely will not be merged).

#113784 has unfortunately stalled though, so somebody needs to pick it back up and resolve the review feedback.

I'll try and find some time to get it moving for 4.8, but I'm pretty swamped with other stuff.
